newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mercenaries train soldiers in Zaire, sources say.
newsitem.headline: Mercenaries train soldiers in Zaire, sources say.

text.p: Foreign mercenaries are training Zairean soldiers in the eastern town of Kisangani, a likely springboard for a thrust against rebels in the east, sources in the French community and senior Zairean dignitaries say.

Zaire's government played down the reports. A spokesman said the only mercenaries he knew of were those serving with the rebels, who since October have seized a swathe of territory along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
There has, however, been little concrete evidence to date of battalions of mercenaries whose presence is signalled almost daily by Zairean newspapers.

French community sources and Zairean dignitaries put the number of mercenaries already in Kisangani at no more than 100. "So far there are only a relatively small group of them in Kisangani," a senior dignitary from the province told Reuters.
Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo's spokesman, Sombo Dibele, dismissed reports of mercenaries as rumours.
"I have no knowledge of this presence of mercenaries. The only mercenaries I know of operating on Zairean soil are fighting with (rebel leader) Laurent Kabila," he said.
The French Le Monde newspaper on Tuesday reported several hundred European and African mercenaries were assembling in the east to help stem advances by the Rwanda-backed rebels.

The daily said the force numbered between 200 and 300 and was expected to grow rapidly when more men leave Europe in two weeks to join South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican soldiers of fortune on the spot.
Kabila accuses France of fighting with the Zairean army and says up to 1,000 French soldiers have been sent to Kisangani. France denies the charge.

Zaire's defence minister said last week that the army would soon be ready for a devastating counter-attack. Mutinous troops who wreaked havoc on civilians after fleeing the conflict would be punished by war councils and removed from the army, he added.
Military sources say that having cleaned up the army as best it can the senior command intends to go to war with a hard core of 6,000 better trained and disciplined troops.
A senior dignitary from the Upper Zaire region said on Tuesday that a band of several hundred mutinous soldiers continued to pillage and terrorise civilians in his province.
The French sources said France had given token support to Zaire's army in recent weeks but not enough to make a real difference in a battle to reconquer territory.
Foreign intermediaries were being used to pay Zairean soldiers in Kisangani, they added.
